content: Ofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic that works by inhibiting bacterial DNA gyrase, which prevents DNA replication, transcription, repair, recombination, and transposition, ultimately leading to bacterial cell death. It is primarily excreted unchanged in the urine (up to 80%) and to a lesser extent in feces (4-8%). The half-life of ofloxacin is approximately 4-5 hours. It should not be taken with antacids or dairy products, as these can interfere with its absorption. When used as an ophthalmic solution (e.g., brand name Ocuflox), ofloxacin is indicated for the treatment of bacterial eye infections. It is not effective against other types of eye infections. To apply the eye drops, wash your hands thoroughly, avoid wearing contact lenses during treatment, and tilt your head back while pulling down the lower eyelid to create a pouch. Administer one drop directly into the eye, close your eyes gently for 1-2 minutes, and apply light pressure to the inner corner of the eye to prevent drainage. Avoid blinking or rubbing your eyes after application. If using other eye medications, wait at least 5 minutes before applying them. Use the medication regularly and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve. Common side effects of the ophthalmic solution include temporary stinging or burning upon application, blurred vision, eye discomfort, itching, redness, dryness, tearing, a sensation of a foreign body in the eye, or light sensitivity. Prolonged or repeated use may lead to secondary fungal eye infections. Serious allergic reactions are rare but possible. If you experience severe symptoms such as difficulty breathing or swelling, seek immediate medical attention. Ofloxacin may interact with other medications, potentially altering their effects or increasing the risk of side effects. For example, it can increase the QTc interval when used with certain drugs, raising the risk of arrhythmias. It may also affect the metabolism or clearance of other drugs, such as temazepam, triazolam, or warfarin. Additionally, co-administration with polyvalent cation-containing products (e.g., magnesium, zinc) can reduce its bioavailability. To minimize interactions, administer ofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after such products. During pregnancy, ofloxacin should only be used if clearly needed, as its safety has not been fully established. It is excreted in breast milk, so breastfeeding should be discontinued if the drug is used. Store the medication at room temperature and discard it if it changes color, becomes cloudy, or develops particles. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet; dispose of it properly when it is no longer needed. If a dose is missed, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. In case of overdose, seek immediate medical attention or contact a poison control center. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about ofloxacin. Always consult your healthcare provider for personalized medical advice and complete information about this medication.
